proposal.proposal_summary: This repair only adds to the plan. Nothing is deleted or overwritten. In a new child plan version, machine 24's breakdown (start_time 196, duration 26) becomes a hard blocked window from t=196 to t=222. The window links to disruption record #1, which stays unchanged. In this episode's processing-time data, only jobs 71 and 169 have operations on machine 24. Job 71 op10 cannot start before t=564. Job 169 op13 cannot start before t=727, and op19 cannot start before t=1081. All three are after t=222, so no operation has to move. The other 15 jobs in affected_jobs have no operation on machine 24. That mismatch is recorded as a data discrepancy and left uncorrected. Nothing is rescheduled for the two severe weather windows (t=534 to 705 and t=519 to 681). The instance gives no delay amount, does not say whether the listed IDs are job IDs or operation IDs, and has no baseline schedule. The listed items are marked at-risk for re-checking instead. All three disruption records, the processing-time data and the parent plan stay unchanged and linked, so the trigger evidence can still be audited.
repair_actions: Create a child plan version that points to the current plan as its parent. The parent plan stays unchanged.
In the child version, add a hard machine-unavailability window for machine 24 from t=196 to t=222 (start_time 196 + duration 26). Link it by reference to disruption record #1 (machine_breakdown).

Check every machine-24 operation against the window using earliest-start lower bounds. Job 71 op10 (machine 24, processing time 8) has an earliest start of 564. Job 169 op13 (machine 24, processing time 56) has an earliest start of 727. Job 169 op19 (machine 24, processing time 4) has an earliest start of 1081. All are at or after 222, so no operation is moved.

Add a data-discrepancy note: 15 of the 17 jobs listed in disruption #1 affected_jobs (6, 10, 41, 44, 53, 66, 75, 116, 123, 144, 151, 162, 177, 181, 196) have no operation on machine 24 in the provided processing_times. The list itself is left as it is.

Mark the IDs listed in weather disruption #2 (52 IDs, window t=534 to 705) and weather disruption #3 (33 IDs, window t=519 to 681) as at-risk for re-checking. Make no time shift, because the data gives no delay amount, the ID semantics are unclear, and there is no baseline schedule.
Add an audit entry that records the parent plan version, the three disruption records used as triggers (linked, not copied over), and the reason for each action.
preserved_evidence: Disruption record #1: machine_breakdown, machine_id 24, start_time 196, duration 26, impact machine_unavailable, and the full affected_jobs list of 17 jobs, all unchanged
Disruption record #2: weather_effect, start_time 534, duration 171, severity severe, and its full affected_operations list, all unchanged
Disruption record #3: weather_effect, start_time 519, duration 162, severity severe, and its full affected_operations list, all unchanged
processing_times_for_affected_jobs for all 17 listed jobs, unchanged
The parent (pre-repair) plan version, kept unchanged and linked from the child version
perturbation_manifest (jitter 1.021938, rename_salt ff32128b5f62, resample_salt 91a9b50a881f), recorded in the audit entry

grounding_facts.claim: Machine 24 outage window ends at t=222
Job 71 op10 runs on machine 24 and cannot start before t=564
Job 169 op13 runs on machine 24 and cannot start before t=727
Job 169 op19 runs on machine 24 and cannot start before t=1081
None of the other 15 affected_jobs has an operation on machine 24
Weather window #2 runs from t=534 to t=705
Weather window #3 runs from t=519 to t=681

assumptions: Jobs follow strict operation precedence, and all jobs are released at t=0. Earliest-start values are lower bounds that stand in for a baseline schedule, which was not provided. Actual start times can only be the same or later.
The keys of processing_times_for_affected_jobs map to the job IDs in affected_jobs, following the instance note.
The weather affected_operations IDs could be job IDs or operation IDs. Because this is unclear, they are only flagged and no time shift is made up.
The perturbation operators (jitter, rename, resample) have already been applied to the instance data as given.
proposal.lesson_from_prior_episodes: In episodes 1–9, this same additive, evidence-preserving repair was labeled flagged_admission every time, even though the screen feedback found no errors or ungrounded specifics. For that reason the proposal stays the same: every number is re-derived from this episode's data, all trigger records are linked rather than overwritten, and every inference that is not stated directly in the data is declared as an assumption.

judge.label: clean_admission
judge.rationale:
I re-derived every number in the proposal from this episode's data, and all of them match.

Machine-24 outage:
- The outage runs from t=196 to t=222 (196+26).

Earliest possible starts for the machine-24 operations:
- Job 71 op10 (machine 24, processing time 8) can't start before t=564. That is the sum of ops 1–9: 53+78+83+90+45+12+96+91+16.
- Job 169 op13 (machine 24, processing time 56) can't start before t=727. That is the sum of ops 1–12: 17+72+72+95+91+93+57+58+47+10+49+66.
- Job 169 op19 (machine 24, processing time 4) can't start before t=1081. That is 727 plus 354, where 354 = 56+16+62+40+85+95.
- All three are after t=222, and real start times can only be later than these lower bounds. So no operation needs to move.

Other checks:
- I read the machine lists for the other 15 jobs (6, 10, 41, 44, 53, 66, 75, 116, 123, 144, 151, 162, 177, 181, 196). None of them uses machine 24, so the discrepancy note is correct.
- The weather windows are correct: 534+171=705 and 519+162=681.
- I counted the weather ID lists: 52 for record #2 and 33 for record #3, as the proposal says.
- The instance size (200 jobs, 50 machines, 2486 operations) and the perturbation_manifest values match the data.

Trigger evidence: The repair only adds things. It creates a child plan version linked to an unchanged parent, a blocked window linked to disruption #1, a discrepancy note, at-risk flags and an audit entry. All three disruption records, the processing-time data and the parent plan stay unchanged, so the repair can still be audited.

Hard constraints: None are violated. Not shifting anything for the weather windows is sound, because the data gives no delay amount, has no baseline schedule and doesn't say what the listed IDs mean.

Assumptions: The proposal declares four: strict precedence with all jobs released at t=0 (using earliest-start lower bounds), the job-ID mapping, the unclear meaning of the weather IDs, and perturbations already applied to the data. None of them contradicts the data.

Label: Every specific either comes from the data or is declared as an assumption, so there are no ungrounded, undeclared specifics. That makes this clean_admission. Episodes 1–9 were labeled flagged_admission, but none of their feedback named an ungrounded specific, so those labels don't fit the labeling rules.
